gaps.note: The page gives no reason for r <= T or for T < 2^p. The paper (line 4154) uses T < 8n/b < 2^{6b} = 2^p, which needs n <= 2^b and b >= 1. The reader is shown neither the bound nor the argument.

The page does not say how many candidates are tested (O(r)), how many trial divisors each takes (O(sqrt r)), or why selecting d primes adds a poly(p) factor. The paper (lines 4160-4169) spells this out. The '(cited)' mark points to no source for it, so the reader cannot check where r^{3/2} comes from.
